fullName: Polarization Modulation Spectroscopy: polarized hard X-rays for magnetism at extreme pressure, cold and field

status2026.detail: The APS beamline directory, read 2026-10-08, lists POLAR as operational and accepting general users with on-site and remote access. First light came in late 2024 or early 2025 after installation in 2023 to 2024, according to APS News in June 2026 and the September and October 2024 APS-U updates. A University of Wisconsin team studying flexomagnetism first used it in run 2025-1, January to May 2025. APS News in March 2025 still described commissioning; the June 2025 article reports the first users. POLAR was absent from the August 2025 list of feature beamlines awaiting first experiments. In June 2026 its lead engineer described 'experiments across three instrument stations'. Project completion, CD-4, was announced in February 2026. The September 2026 ID table still lists two planar 3.0 cm undulators. Planned SCAPE sources cover 2.7 to 27 keV, with fully circular polarization only in the first harmonic. The permanent-magnet alternative is a 1 m X-undulator prototype design starting at 2.6 keV. Neither is installed. Crystal phase retarders therefore provide circular and vertical-linear polarization over about 2.7 to 14 keV.

tagline: Researchers measure element-specific magnetism with polarized X-rays at pressures of millions of atmospheres.
summary: At POLAR, polarized X-ray absorption is measured to determine magnetism in individual elements. The beamline extends 78 m at Sector 4 of Argonne's Advanced Photon Source, APS. X-rays emitted by the planar undulators have an electric field oscillating horizontally. After transmission through thin diamond plates, the field rotates around the beam axis, giving circular polarization. Researchers repeatedly tilt the plates with piezoelectric actuators to reverse the circular polarization. At an absorption edge, where inner electrons are excited, a magnetic material absorbs opposite circular polarizations differently. Researchers use this difference, a fraction of a percent to a few percent, to determine the element's magnetization along the beam. The focal spot is 100 to 400 nm for samples between diamond tips at pressures up to 3 megabars, about three million atmospheres. Measurements combine pressure with fields up to 9 tesla and temperatures down to 1.4 K above absolute zero. First users arrived in 2025.

whatAPSUEnables.text: Samples squeezed between diamond tips require a small X-ray beam. The upgraded electron source is about 19 times narrower horizontally. The 2021 flat-beam design gives a root-mean-square width of 14.5 µm instead of 275 µm. The polarized light is focused to 100 to 400 nm, compared with about 15 µm before the upgrade. Smaller samples allow higher pressure. The goal is 6 megabars, compared with about 0.5 megabar for earlier magnetic measurements and 3.6 megabars at Earth's centre. At 10 keV the coherent fraction, whose waves maintain the phase relationship needed for lens-free imaging, is about 200 times larger. This supports magnetic imaging targets of 10 to 50 nm. The planned polarized-flux gain in a 300 nm spot is about 100 times. The 2026 listing gives 3 megabars and 400 nm magnetic imaging. Polarizing undulators remain uninstalled. They would avoid the phase plates' 5 to 30-fold flux loss and extend polarization above 14 keV.
quantitative: The 2021 POLAR town hall gives horizontal electron widths of 275 µm before the upgrade and 14.5 µm in the nominal flat-beam design. These are root-mean-square widths. Angular spread falls from 11 to 2.9 µrad.
The design coherent fraction at 10 keV is 200 times the pre-upgrade value, according to the 2023 POLAR workshop slides and 2021 town hall.

The pre-upgrade 4-ID-D toroid and KB mirrors produced roughly 15 × 15 µm² polarized beams. The listed KB spots are 100 to 200 nm at 4-ID-G and 300 to 400 nm at 4-ID-H. Sources are the 2018 4-ID-D page and 2026 beamline directory.

The 2021 town hall projects about 100 times more flux in roughly 300 nm beams. Adding SCAPE sources would raise polarized and polarized-coherent flux in 100 to 300 nm beams by about 1,000 times. That combines a roughly 100-fold focusing gain with about 10 times more flux than phase plates transmit.

Strempfer et al. 2022 give 1.3 × 10¹³ photons/s at 10 keV in a 114 × 92 nm² KB spot at 4-ID-G, and 2.1 × 10¹³ photons/s in a 414 × 212 nm² KB spot at 4-ID-H. The accepted angular range is 20 × 20 µrad².
Strempfer et al. 2022 give a coherent-mode flux of 1.6 × 10¹² photons/s at 10 keV in a 200 × 200 nm² spot at 4-ID-G, using KB mirrors and a slit.

The 2017 Preliminary Design Report projects focused flux-density gains from lower emittance alone of 50 times at 10 keV and 80 times at 20 keV. At 10 keV that combines 20 times less spot area with 2.5 times better transmission.

Earlier APS-led magnetic circular dichroism measurements typically reached about 0.5 Mbar, with about 1 Mbar a maximum in most cases. The 2026 directory lists 3 Mbar at 4-ID-H. The 2021 town hall sets a 6 Mbar goal, near the 6 to 7 Mbar static-compression limit. These comparisons also use the 2017 Preliminary Design Report and 2018 4-ID-D high-pressure page.
Argonne news in February 2026 and the 2021 POLAR town hall give an APS-U design brightness gain of up to about 500 times.

techniques.name: X-ray magnetic circular dichroism
techniques.text: X-ray magnetic circular dichroism, XMCD, measures the difference in absorption of left- and right-circularly polarized X-rays at one element's absorption edge. A difference requires a net alignment of that element's magnetic moments. Its size and sign measure their strength and direction along the beam. With hard X-rays the effect is typically 0.1 to 6% of the absorption step. The design calls for reversing the polarization 13 to 15 times a second. Lock-in detection selects the signal that reverses at that frequency, with a target sensitivity of ten parts per million. At the L edges of 4d and 5d metals, equations called sum rules separate spin and orbital magnetism. At the K edges of 3d metals and L edges of rare earths, XMCD comes from magnetism induced in outer electrons and is interpreted more qualitatively. Actinide L edges above the phase plates' roughly 14 keV limit require a future polarizing undulator.

techniques.name: X-ray linear and magnetic linear dichroism
techniques.text: X-ray linear dichroism, XLD, compares absorption of horizontally and vertically polarized X-rays. It measures directional differences in electron orbitals and ferroelectric distortions. Its magnetic counterpart, XMLD, measures the axis of magnetic alignment. It also works in antiferromagnets, where opposing neighbouring moments cancel and produce no circular dichroism. POLAR sets its phase retarders as a half-wave plate to make vertical polarization. The vertically polarized fraction is about 80% at low energies and 95% at high energies. The 4-ID-H magnet supplies a field of up to 1 tesla across the beam for XMLD.

techniques.name: Polarized X-ray absorption near-edge / fine structure
techniques.text: X-ray absorption near-edge structure, XANES, measures how absorption changes as the X-ray energy passes through an element's absorption edge. X-ray absorption fine structure, XAFS, also measures oscillations above the edge. Charge state, called valence, and local atomic surroundings are determined from these spectra. Pressure can move an electron from a rare earth's localized 4f shell into conducting states shared through the material. Measurements address such valence changes in ytterbium, europium, cerium and uranium, including mixed valence and the Kondo effect. In the Kondo effect, conduction electrons screen a local magnetic moment. Orbital occupancy in 5d oxides under pressure is also measured. Spectra are recorded in transmission through the diamond anvils or by fluorescence, usually alongside magnetic circular dichroism on the same sample.

techniques.name: X-ray resonant magnetic scattering / diffraction
techniques.text: X-ray resonant magnetic scattering, XRMS, measures crystal diffraction with the X-ray energy tuned to an element's absorption edge. A repeating magnetic pattern can produce weak diffraction spots absent from the atomic lattice alone. Antiferromagnets, for example, have alternating magnetic moments. Resonance increases this scattering and makes it element-specific. POLAR uses the 4-ID-G Huber diffractometer. Its detector arm has two branches 25° apart, carrying an area detector and a polarization analyzer. The analyzer separates scattered light polarized perpendicular, σ, and parallel, π, to the scattering plane. Samples can be cooled to 4 K, placed in a ±2 T magnet, compressed in mini diamond cells to 20 GPa, or strained.

techniques.name: X-ray resonant magnetic reflectivity
techniques.text: X-ray resonant magnetic reflectivity, XRMR, measures reflection from thin films at shallow angles with polarized X-rays. Reflections from successive interfaces interfere. Their intensity as a function of angle depends on magnetism through the layers. Measurements are sensitive to an interface only an atomic layer thick. POLAR measures the specular reflection, where incident and reflected angles match, and nearby diffuse scattering using circular dichroism. An in-vacuum setup reaches the ruthenium, rhodium and palladium L edges at 2.75 to 3.4 keV in fields up to 2 tesla.

techniques.name: Dichroic ptychography and tomography
techniques.text: Coherent diffractive imaging reconstructs an image from scattered X-rays without an image-forming lens. In ptychography, a coherent focused beam scans overlapping areas of the sample. A detector records the diffraction pattern at each position, and a computer reconstructs a sample image consistent with the patterns. Circular polarization tuned to a magnetic absorption edge makes that image sensitive to magnetic domains. Rotating the sample and repeating the scans yields a 3D map of magnetization direction, called vector tomography. POLAR combines 100 to 200 nm coherent beams with a precision air-bearing stage. Detector positions at 2.7, 4 and 10 m are planned. The imaging goal is 10 to 50 nm. The 2026 directory lists 400 nm for dichroic imaging. Its 3D reconstruction software has been demonstrated on MAX IV data from Sweden; a POLAR demonstration has not been reported.

techniques.name: Spectroscopy in the diamond anvil cell at extreme pressure, low temperature and high field
techniques.text: The extreme-conditions instrument combines a diamond anvil cell with low temperature and high field. A small sample sits between two flat diamond tips, called culets, in a non-magnetic copper-beryllium cell. Helium-filled membranes control the pressure remotely while the cell is cold. Diamond transmits hard X-rays but absorbs substantially at the 5 to 9 keV edges of transition metals and rare earths. At the iron edge, 1 mm transmits about 10% of the beam. Perforated or partially perforated anvils leave only 0.1 to 0.2 mm in the beam path. Ruby fluorescence measures pressure below 100 GPa, equivalent to 1 megabar. Above it, researchers use the diamond's Raman signal or diffraction from a gold, silver or platinum marker. Double-stage or toroidal anvils are planned for multi-megabar work.

scienceCases.title: Magnetism and valence of rare earths and actinides at multi-megabar pressure
scienceCases.text: Compression changes atomic separations and can rearrange electrons, suppress magnetism or produce superconductivity. In rare-earth and actinide materials, two effects compete. Conduction electrons couple magnetic moments on different atoms through the RKKY interaction. They also screen individual moments through the Kondo effect. Targets include ytterbium's magnetic 4f¹³ and non-magnetic 4f¹⁴ states, superconductivity near mixed valence, plutonium, and the unresolved hidden order of URu₂Si₂. At 4-ID-H, POLAR uses absorption spectroscopy and magnetic circular dichroism at rare-earth and 5d L edges. Its range is 1.4 to 300 K and up to 9 T, with a pressure goal of 6 megabars. Actinide M edges at 3.3 to 4 keV are within the current polarization range. Their L edges at about 16 to 22 keV require the planned polarizing undulator.

scienceCases.title: High-pressure hydrides and superconductivity
scienceCases.text: Lanthanum hydride, LaH₁₀, superconducts at up to about 250 K, or −23 °C, under pressures of around 1.7 to 1.9 megabars. Samples at these pressures are only micrometres across and require smaller beams. POLAR's 0.1 to 0.4 µm polarized beams and megabar diamond-cell instruments are intended to measure the electronic and magnetic structure of these hydrides and related sulfides. Iron hydrides are another target. Researchers want to determine whether magnetism contributes to superconductivity in these materials.

scienceCases.title: Quantum materials under pressure
scienceCases.text: Pressure changes electron motion and interactions without introducing chemical impurities. It can turn an insulator into a metal or change magnetic order. Proposed measurements concern 4d and 5d oxides, including Sr₂IrO₄-type iridates and honeycomb materials proposed as Kitaev quantum spin liquids. In a spin liquid, magnetic moments remain disordered despite interactions between them. POLAR's predecessor, 4-ID-D, measured iridium-edge magnetic circular dichroism in a diamond cell at 8 GPa and 11 K. Other targets include insulator-to-metal transitions in stiff transition-metal oxides and spin freezing in frustrated magnets. In those magnets, competing interactions prevent all neighbouring moments from adopting their preferred alignment. Short-range magnetic order produces weak diffuse scattering, so these measurements need high incident flux.

scienceCases.title: Imaging magnetic, chiral and ferroelectric domains
scienceCases.text: Magnets and ferroelectrics contain regions of uniform orientation, called domains, and more complex arrangements such as skyrmions and polar vortices. Some could be used to store data. Images of these structures within a crystal are reconstructed from coherent polarized diffraction. Proposed measurements include magnetic domains, antiferromagnetic domains measured through linear dichroism, skyrmion strings and polar vortices. Resolution targets are 10 to 50 nm for reconstruction and about 100 nm for direct scanning. The cited demonstrations were made elsewhere. Ferroelectric incommensurate spin crystals in SrRuO₃/PbTiO₃ trilayers were measured at the pre-upgrade 4-ID-D. The 3D magnetization of Nd₂Fe₁₄B pillars was reconstructed from MAX IV data with software now used at POLAR.

scienceCases.title: Strain gradients and flexomagnetism in thin membranes
scienceCases.text: Bending a thin crystal stretches one side and compresses the other. The resulting strain gradient can create magnetism, called flexomagnetism. POLAR's first users, a University of Wisconsin team in the January to May 2025 run, studied this effect in thin materials for microelectronics. A related Wisconsin-Madison group creates strain gradients of about 10⁶ m⁻¹ in GdAuGe films by helium-ion implantation and identifies nanoprobe magnetic circular dichroism as a needed measurement. Gadolinium's L₃ edge at 7.243 keV lies within POLAR's phase-plate range. Connecting the first users to that group is an inference. The group's published nanodiffraction used the National Synchrotron Light Source II, not POLAR.

scienceCases.title: Interfaces and heterostructures at low photon energy
scienceCases.text: A magnetic layer can induce a moment in a neighbouring metal that is otherwise non-magnetic. POLAR measures this interface magnetism element by element. An in-vacuum setup on the 4-ID-G diffractometer reaches the ruthenium, rhodium and palladium L edges at 2.75 to 3.4 keV, as well as the K edges of 3d metals. It supports magnetic circular and linear dichroism and resonant reflectivity in fields up to ±2 T. Targets include proximity-induced moments and 4d and 5d layers with strong spin-orbit coupling, the interaction between spin and orbital motion. Uniaxial-strain and voltage-bias cells are also supported.

scienceCases.title: Magnetic X-ray emission spectroscopy under extreme conditions
scienceCases.text: After a sample absorbs X-rays, it emits X-rays with energies that depend on its electronic and magnetic state. X-ray emission spectroscopy measures this spectrum. The emission depends on local magnetism even when atomic moments have no net alignment. A 2024 US Department of Energy Early Career award to G. Fabbris funds a magnetic X-ray emission spectroscopy instrument, MagXES, at POLAR. The award provides $550,000 a year for five years for new spectrometer designs suited to low temperature, high pressure and high field. The instrument's status in 2026 is unconfirmed.

keyParameters.label: Energy range
keyParameters.value: 2.7 to 27 keV
keyParameters.note: The FDR and SRI 2021 give 2.75 to 27 keV. The public POLAR Bluesky configuration limits the monochromator software to 2.6 to 32 keV.

keyParameters.label: Polarization states
keyParameters.value: Linear-H from the undulators; left/right circular, elliptical and linear-V via diamond phase retarders
keyParameters.note: Source-based switching with SCAPE or an X-undulator remains planned, according to the 2021 town hall and Qian et al. 2024.

keyParameters.label: Phase-retarder energy range
keyParameters.value: About 2.7 to 14 keV
keyParameters.note: The plates are diamond C(111)/(220) and thin Si(111). The 2021 town hall gives the low-energy limit as 2.7 or 2.8 keV. The 2018 4-ID-D page gives earlier ranges of 3.2 to 15 keV for diamond and 2.8 to 3.2 keV for 10 µm silicon.

keyParameters.label: Degree of polarization
keyParameters.value: Pc ≈ ±0.98; vertical Plin ≈ −0.80 at low energy to −0.95 at high energy

keyParameters.label: Helicity modulation
keyParameters.value: About 15 Hz with phase plates in piezo AC mode
keyParameters.note: 15 Hz is the 2021 town-hall design value. The current user-mode frequency is unpublished. Haskel et al. 2007 and the 2018 4-ID-D page give 12.7 to 13 Hz for the older instrument. Srajer 2002 reports up to 40 Hz.

keyParameters.label: Source
keyParameters.value: Two in-line planar hybrid permanent-magnet undulators, upstream APS30#4 and downstream APS30#9, with a phase shifter; λu = 3.0 cm and 79 periods each
keyParameters.note: The 2019 FDR specifies two 2.3 m U30 devices at the straight-section centre.

keyParameters.label: Undulator Keff / first harmonic
keyParameters.value: Keff ≈ 2.62 to 2.64 at a 9.0 mm gap; E1 ≈ 2.54 to 2.56 keV at 6 GeV
keyParameters.note: User minimum gaps are 9.4 mm upstream and 9.1 mm downstream.

keyParameters.label: Source power
keyParameters.value: 10.2 + 10.4 kW total; 214 to 215 kW/mrad² peak per device at 200 mA and minimum gap
keyParameters.note: The 2019 FDR, Chapter 3, gives front-end limits of 21 kW and 590 kW/mrad².

keyParameters.label: Monochromator
keyParameters.value: CINEL vertical-deflecting LN₂-cooled DCM, Si(111) + 6H-SiC(0006), 15.6 mm fixed offset
keyParameters.note: The 15.6 mm offset is from the 2021 town hall. The 2019 FDR specifies horizontal reflection; the later design uses vertical reflection. Strempfer et al. 2022 and the POLAR Bluesky configuration document that change.

keyParameters.label: Energy resolution

keyParameters.label: Mono angular stability spec

The SRI 2021 account does not specify whether a phase plate is included.

insertionDevices.name: Upstream APS30#4
insertionDevices.type: Variable-gap planar hybrid permanent-magnet undulator outside the vacuum chamber
insertionDevices.notes: The device has 79 periods, with 77 effective. Multiplying 79 by 30 mm gives a 2.37 m magnetic length. Minimum gaps are 9.0 mm for the device, 9.17 mm administratively and 9.4 mm for users. Keff is 2.62 and E1 is 2.56 keV. At 200 mA it produces 10.2 kW and a peak density of 214 kW/mrad². This is a full-length reused pre-upgrade magnetic structure; refurbishment details are unpublished. Dejus et al. 2024, Table 1, lists 3.0 cm periods under 'Existing IDs', with 3 full-length and 5 canted devices. New APS-U periods are 1.35, 1.4, 2.1, 2.5 and 2.8 cm, with full-length devices about 2.4 m. The 2019 FDR specification is 'Linear 30 mm, 2 × 2.3 m at SSC'.

insertionDevices.name: Downstream APS30#9
insertionDevices.type: Variable-gap planar hybrid permanent-magnet undulator outside the vacuum chamber
insertionDevices.notes: The device has 79 periods. Minimum gaps are 9.0 mm for the device, 9.06 mm administratively and 9.1 mm for users. Keff is 2.64 and E1 is 2.54 keV. At 200 mA it produces 10.4 kW and a peak density of 215 kW/mrad².

insertionDevices.name: In-line phase shifter S04ID:ILPS with corrector
insertionDevices.notes: This magnet delays the electrons so radiation from both undulators arrives in phase. Dejus et al. 2024 reports 11 phase shifters with correctors installed in in-line sectors. POLAR's Bluesky configuration exposes its controls. Its length is unpublished; zero in the source table denotes that missing value.

insertionDevices.name: SCAPE polarizing undulators, two planned units
insertionDevices.type: Superconducting four-coil crossed-planar undulator with variable polarization
insertionDevices.notes: SCAPE is a planned replacement for both planar sources. Pure circular polarization occurs only in the first harmonic. Higher harmonics produce horizontal or vertical linear light or elliptical light, with a circular fraction adjustable to about 75 to 90% in the PDR. This supplies the proposed 14 to 27 keV range. The FDR gives a conservative 35 mm period and 1.3 m length, with possible 30 mm periods and lengths up to 1.8 m. The PDR gives a 3.0 cm period and 1.5 m length in one roughly 4.5 m cryostat. Switching proposals use alternating orbit deflections of about 30 µrad at up to 10 Hz or undulator-current changes of about 6 A. A 0.5 m NbTi prototype was tested in 2021 with a 30 mm period, 16.5 periods, a 10 mm magnetic gap and 540 A operating current, according to Kasa et al. 2021. The 2021 town hall proposed replacement around 2026. A round vacuum chamber about 6 mm in diameter is required. The September 2026 ID table does not confirm installation.

insertionDevices.name: X-undulator alternative, prototype design
insertionDevices.type: fixed-gap APPLE-X-like pure permanent-magnet undulator with force-compensation arrays
insertionDevices.polarization: Circular, elliptical and linear polarization at any angle
insertionDevices.notes: Four NdFeB Halbach arrays surround an 8.5 mm bore. The round chamber has 6.0 mm inner and 7.5 mm outer diameters. Maximum Keff is 2.6, giving a 2.6 keV minimum energy. Longitudinal array motion adjusts field strength and polarization. A quarter-period motion switches at 1 Hz; a dual-XU detuning proposal gives about 5 Hz. Qian et al. 2024 describes a 1 m prototype design. A 2023 internal research grant funded 'Force-neutral fast polarization switching X-undulator for the POLAR beamline', as listed in Haskel's 2024 CV. It is not installed.

source.canting: The two planar undulators are collinear in the 4-ID straight, separated by a phase shifter. The 2019 FDR and September 2026 ID table confirm this configuration. Before the upgrade, canted sources served two directions. Srajer 2002 describes a 12.8 cm-period circularly polarizing electromagnetic undulator for soft-X-ray 4-ID-C and a 3.3 cm Undulator A for hard-X-ray 4-ID-D. By 2018, the 4-ID-D page listed a 2.4 m SmCo device with a 3.5 cm period. APS News 2020 describes the conversion of the whole straight to POLAR.
source.frontEnd: The windowless APS-U high-heat-load front end uses differential pumping. Its limits are 21 kW total power and 590 kW/mrad² peak density, from the 2019 FDR, Chapter 3. The design derives from the 28-ID HHL front end. In order, its elements are LPPS, the storage-ring valve, burn-through mask BTFM1, fixed mask FM2, a collimator, GRID XBPM, FM3, photon shutter PS2 with an intensity monitor, redundant shutters SS1/SS2, the wall collimator, front-end valve, exit mask with XBPM2, exit collimator and beamline isolation valve. The exit mask is 2 × 2 mm, horizontal by vertical, at about 25.4 m. The 5 × 5 mm exit collimator is at about 26.1 m. With the undulators tuned to 2.8 keV in linear polarization, total power is about 16 kW. The white-beam slits at 27 m receive about 512 W/mm².
source.sourceSizeAndDivergence: FDR Table 1.1 gives design electron-source sizes and divergences. The 324-bunch brightness mode has 42 pm emittance, σx = 14.7 µm, σx' = 2.8 µrad, σy = 3.2 µm and σy' = 1.3 µrad. The 48-bunch timing mode has 32 pm effective emittance, σx = 12.9 µm, σx' = 2.5 µrad, σy = 8.8 µm and σy' = 3.7 µrad. The 2021 town hall instead quotes σx = 14.5 µm and σx' = 2.9 µrad, compared with 275 µm and 11 µrad before the upgrade. For L ≈ 2.4 m at 10 keV, calculated approximate single-electron photon terms are σr ≈ √(2λL)/4π ≈ 2 µm and σr' ≈ √(λ/2L) ≈ 5 µrad. The sources occupy about ±1.3 m around the straight centre. The 2017 PDR ray traces with sources at ±1 m give slightly asymmetric KB spots, reduced by defining slits.

components.name: Upstream undulator APS30#4
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. the centre of the upstream device, inferred because no coordinate is published. Two ~2.4 m devices and a phase shifter share the ~5 m straight section.
components.text: This 2.4-metre undulator uses alternating magnets to bend the path of 6 GeV electrons 79 times. Radiation from successive bends combines into a narrow X-ray beam with a horizontally oscillating electric field. The 3.0 cm magnet period produces a first harmonic near 2.6 keV at minimum gap. Higher odd harmonics, at odd multiples of that energy, extend to 27 keV. Its magnet structure was reused from the original APS.

components.name: In-line phase shifter + corrector
components.distanceNote: Approximate and inferred: between the two undulators, near the centre of the straight section.
components.text: This adjustable magnet changes the electron path between the two undulators. The resulting delay makes radiation from the second device arrive in phase with radiation from the first, so their intensities combine constructively. Its setting follows the undulator gap. Corrector magnets maintain the orbit. The upgrade installed 11 such units in sectors with two in-line undulators.

specs.purpose: constructive interference of the two undulators

components.name: Downstream undulator APS30#9
components.distanceNote: Approximate and inferred: the centre of the downstream device.
components.text: This second undulator has the same design as the first and lies on the same axis. Together they roughly double the flux, with horizontal linear polarization. Planned Superconducting Arbitrarily Polarizing Emitter undulators, called SCAPE, or a permanent-magnet X-undulator could replace the pair and generate circular polarization directly. Neither was installed in September 2026.

components.name: High-heat-load front end, windowless
components.distanceNote: The schematic places one unit at 20 m. The front end extends from about 13 m to about 26 m in the first optics enclosure, crossing the ratchet shielding wall near 23.6 to 24.4 m. These extents follow the 2021 plan and elevation. Most individual positions are unpublished. The last elements follow the elevation, with photon shutter near 22.2 m, tandem safety shutters near 22.7 to 23.4 m and wall collimator within the wall. Upstream order follows the final design.
components.text: The front end connects the accelerator to the beamline, mostly inside the concrete shielding tunnel. Water-cooled masks absorb the outer beam, monitors measure beam position, and shutters block it for access to the first hutch. Its X-ray power limit is 21 kW. Differential pumping separates its vacuum from the beamline vacuum without a beryllium window. This avoids window absorption and disturbance of the coherent beam.

components.name: Front-end exit mask, with XBPM2
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.16.
components.text: The 2 × 2 mm opening in this water-cooled copper block transmits the central beam. The block absorbs the outer beam as heat. An integrated position monitor checks beam centring. The block sits on the final front-end table inside the first hutch.

components.name: Front-end exit collimator
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.16.
components.text: This tungsten block limits the path of bremsstrahlung through a 5 × 5 mm opening. Bremsstrahlung is high-energy radiation emitted when stored electrons interact with residual gas. A downstream stop absorbs radiation that passes through the opening. The upgrade narrowed the opening for beamlines whose monochromators produce small beam offsets.

components.name: High-heat-load white-beam slits, 4ID-SL-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.16; the 2021 plan shows the slit at ~26.8 to 27.6 m, scaled.
components.text: Four tungsten-edged jaws limit the white beam, which contains the full spectrum, and reduce the heat reaching downstream optics. With the undulators tuned to 2.8 keV, incident power density is about 512 W/mm², roughly eight times the solar surface value. A 0.92 × 0.92 mm opening accepts the full 2.8 keV cone but transmits only 432 W of roughly 16 kW total power. The usual opening is 0.5 × 0.5 mm.

specs.maxPowerThroughSlit: 432 W, 0.92 × 0.92 mm² at 27 m, undulators tuned to 2.8 keV; FDR Table 4.15

components.name: White-beam mirrors M1 and M2, flat and bendable
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.16, both mirrors share one vessel. The 2021 plan shows the tank at ~27.6 to 29.2 m, scaled.
components.text: Two polished silicon mirrors reflect the beam sideways and back at grazing angles of 3 milliradians, or 0.17°. The emerging beam is parallel to the incident beam and offset about 4 mm. Each mirror has silicon, rhodium and platinum stripes with different reflection cut-off energies. Choosing a stripe rejects higher harmonics. The flat first mirror absorbs 254 W at 2.8 keV. Bending the second mirror compensates for thermal deformation of the first mirror and the monochromator crystal.

components.name: Photon mask / pink-beam stop, 4ID-PM-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.16.
components.text: This cooled block absorbs beam that passes straight through the mirror pair. Only the reflected beam continues to the monochromator. Its filtered spectrum is called pink beam.

components.name: Beam-viewing flags + cameras, 4-ID-A
components.distanceNote: Approximate; shown at the post-mirror flag. The Bluesky configuration defines two 4-ID-A flag cameras, PostMirrBeam, between the mirror tank, ending ~29.2 m, and the DCM vessel, starting ~30.15 m on the 2021 plan, so ~29.7 m and PostMonoBeam, after the DCM, ~31.3 m. Positions are not published.
components.text: These fluorescent screens move into the beam and emit visible light where X-rays strike. Cameras record the beam position after the mirrors and after the monochromator. Staff use them to align the optics and check changes of coating stripe or crystal.

components.name: Vertical double-crystal monochromator with silicon and silicon carbide
components.distanceNote: Centre of the DCM vessel on the 2021 'Sector 4 2024' plan and elevation, ~30.15 to 31.05 m, scaled; drawn as a drum ~0.9 m across in the elevation. FDR Table 4.16 listed 30.0 m when the DCM was still specified as horizontal-deflecting; as built it is vertical-deflecting.
components.text: Two crystals select an X-ray energy by Bragg reflection. Their atomic spacing and angle determine the reflected wavelength, with an energy width of about one part in 7,000. Rotation scans the energy through an absorption edge for magnetic measurements. Liquid-nitrogen cooling limits thermal deformation. Vertical reflection keeps horizontally polarized light perpendicular to the reflection plane, called σ geometry. A second silicon-carbide pair near 2.8 keV is intended for future source-generated polarization. Its installation and use are unpublished.

specs.geometry: vertical deflection: linear-H light reflects in σ geometry
specs.SiC crystals: Silicon carbide is intended for source-generated polarization near 2.8 keV. Si(111) reflects near 45° there, suppressing vertical π polarization. 6H-SiC(0006) reflects at 61.4°.

components.name: Monochromatic-beam slits, 4ID-SL-2
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.16 gives 31.1 m; the 2021 plan shows a small device at ~31.2 m, just downstream of the as-built DCM tank, used here.
components.text: These jaws limit the single-energy beam after the monochromator. They block stray and scattered radiation before it reaches the polarization optics.

components.name: Collimators and white-beam stop
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.16: secondary collimator 31.3 m, photon mask/WB stop 31.7 m, primary bremsstrahlung collimator 32.0 m. Behind the as-built DCM the 2021 plan shows these small items ~0.25 m further downstream, ~31.55, 32.0 and 32.3 m; the model uses the plan values, centred on the WB stop.
components.text: A tungsten stop absorbs beam that travels straight through the crystals. Collimators block stray bremsstrahlung. The monochromator shifts the useful beam vertically by 15.6 mm, allowing it to pass the stop and leave the first hutch.

components.name: Diamond phase retarders, quarter-wave plates
components.distanceNote: Centre of the tank on the 2021 plan, ~33.0 to 33.9 m, scaled; two plate stages drawn as circles. FDR Table 4.16: 33.2 m. This is the existing 4-ID-D tank, reused.
components.text: Thin diamond plates change horizontal linear polarization to circular polarization. A plate set one to two hundredths of a degree away from its reflection angle delays two perpendicular polarization components by different amounts. With the reflection plane at 45° to the incident polarization, a quarter-wave delay produces circular polarization. Tilting to the other side reverses the handedness. With two plates, the output can be vertically polarized. A piezo actuator reverses the tilt about 15 times a second in the design, with about 98% circular polarization. The plates work only up to about 14 keV and reduce flux by a factor of 5 to 30.

specs.plates: pr1, pr2: C(111)/C(220) diamond; pr3: Si(111)
specs.principle: Bragg-transmission quarter-wave plate, Hirano et al. 1993; diamond plates after Lang & Srajer, 1995
specs.Quarter-wave offset: ~42″ at 10 keV, ~80″ at 8 keV off Bragg, 500 µm C(111), calculated
specs.fluxCost: ×5 to 30 flux loss; 5 to 30% intensity asymmetry between helicities

components.name: Monochromatic station shutter, 4ID-SH-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.16; the 2021 plan shows it at ~34.2 to 35.5 m.
components.text: The personnel safety system controls this shutter. It transmits beam from the optics hutch to 4-ID-B only after downstream hutches have been searched and locked.

components.name: Shielded beam transport, 4-ID-A → 4-ID-B
components.distanceNote: Spans ~36.1 to 50.5 m on the 2021 plan, scaled; midpoint given. Pipe stands at ~37.8, 39.0, 41.2, 43.3, 45.3, 46.5 and 48.8 m.
components.text: A lead-shielded 14-metre vacuum pipe carries the beam across the experiment-hall floor. The shielding permits people to use the surrounding floor during beam operation. Supports stand every few metres. The pipe passes an older mini-hutch before entering 4-ID-B.

components.name: 4-ID-B entrance slits, bslt
components.distanceNote: Approximate. The FDR places a mono slit, SL-3 just upstream of the toroids, 47.3 m in the FDR layout; the as-built toroids are at 53.7 m. Position inferred.
components.text: These jaws limit the beam entering the focusing optics in 4-ID-B. The opening determines the accepted flux and influences the focal spot. Their location is inferred from the design component order.

components.name: Toroidal focusing mirror M3, bendable
components.distanceNote: From the 2021 town-hall slide 'Reflectivities/cut-offs', which places the toroidal double mirrors at 53.7 and 54.5 m.
components.text: This bendable coated mirror focuses the beam to about 30 × 5 µm for experiments requiring high flux over a larger area. Its curvature moves the focus to the 4-ID-G diffractometer at 67.2 m or the 4-ID-H magnet at 73.3 m. Its coating also rejects higher harmonics. It retracts when the smaller-spot optics are used.

specs.stripes: Pd sagittal cylinder; Si and Pt flats, SRI 2021

components.name: Cylinder/flat mirror M4
components.distanceNote: From the same 2021 town-hall slide, mirrors at 53.7 and 54.5 m.
components.text: This mirror completes the focusing and returns the beam parallel to its original path, with a lateral offset of a few millimetres. Palladium, silicon and platinum stripes combine with the upstream mirror coatings to reject higher harmonics over 2.7 to 27 keV.

specs.stripes: Pd flat; Si and Pt sagittal cylinders, SRI 2021

components.name: Post-toroid beam-viewing flag, 4-ID-B
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. just downstream of the M4 vessel, 54.5 m; inferred from the device name only.
components.text: A fluorescent screen and camera record the beam after the focusing mirrors during alignment. Its position is inferred from the device name.

components.name: Diamond vacuum window
components.distanceNote: Approximate. A small component on the 2021 plan ~0.8 m after M4, the FDR window was 0.8 m after M4. The FDR specified 'Be or diamond'; Bluesky confirms a diamond window with x/y stages in 4-ID-B.
components.text: A thin diamond window separates the ultra-high-vacuum optics from the experiment section. It transmits X-rays with little disturbance of their phase relationship, preserving coherence for imaging. It is mounted on motorized stages. Diamond was chosen instead of beryllium.

components.name: In-line X-ray polarimeter
components.distanceNote: Approximate. Placed on the 4-ID-B optics table, ~57.5 to 60 m on the 2021 plan following the FDR component order; the FDR position, 53.4 m predates the toroid move.
components.text: A retractable foil scatters beam through 90° to two perpendicular detectors. Scattering is weakest along the electric-field direction, so their intensity ratio measures linear polarization and its axis. Rotation around the beam completes the measurement. For fully polarized light, the circular fraction follows from the linear fraction. A phase plate used as an analyzer gives a direct measurement.

components.name: Diamond XBPM / TetrAMM, 4-ID-B
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. FDR component order, scaled to the 2021 plan.
components.text: This diamond sensor measures beam position with little absorption. Its signal controls piezo actuators on the monochromator's second crystal, with a directional stability target of 0.1 µrad. Stations B, G and H have separate feedback loops.

components.name: In-vacuum optical chopper
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. FDR component order, scaled to the 2021 plan.
components.text: A rotating slotted wheel interrupts the beam up to 4,000 times a second. Electronics compare illuminated and blocked intervals to subtract dark current. This matters for the ten-parts-per-million magnetic-signal target. One lock-in measurement follows the chopper frequency; another follows the slower polarization reversal to measure dichroism.

specs.use: double lock-in: dark current at the chopper frequency, dichroism at the helicity frequency

components.name: Attenuators / filters, 4-ID-B
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. FDR component order, scaled to the 2021 plan.
components.text: Metal foils move into the beam to reduce flux in steps. They protect detectors and radiation-sensitive samples during alignment and occupy a standard APS filter box.

components.name: Bendable KB mirrors 'KB3', 2 T station
components.distanceNote: Approximate. Inferred from the 2021 plan table position upstream of the electromagnet; FDR: 55.1 m relative to the magnet at 55.8 m.
components.text: Two bendable Kirkpatrick-Baez mirrors focus in perpendicular directions onto the 2-tesla electromagnet station. Changing their curvature adjusts the spot size. The 2017 design specifies a minimum of about 10 µm; the as-built spot is unpublished.

specs.focus: down to ~10 µm, PDR 2017 design value; as-built value not published

components.name: Incident-intensity monitor I0, 4-ID-B
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. FDR component order, scaled to the 2021 plan.
components.text: An ion chamber or photodiode measures incident X-ray intensity through a current amplifier. Dividing the transmitted intensity by this value compensates for changes in the incident beam during absorption measurements.

components.name: 2 T electromagnet station, existing
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate, scaled from the 2021 Sector 4 plan with ±0.3 m uncertainty. The older final-design layout placed it at 55.8 m.
components.text: This water-cooled electromagnet came from 4-ID-D. Its field can be ramped and reversed without liquid helium. It supports films, crystals and lightly compressed samples, with up to 2 T at small pole gaps and about 0.8 T around a diamond anvil cell. A flow cryostat provides temperatures above 10 K. The magnet is configured in control software but absent from the 2026 endstation directory. Its availability to users is unconfirmed.

specs.field: up to 2 T, ≈0.8 T with DAC gap

components.name: Transmission photodiode I, 4-ID-B
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. a feature on the 2021 plan just downstream of the magnet.
components.text: This photodiode measures X-rays transmitted through the sample and magnet. Absorption increases at an element's absorption edge. The small change in transmission when polarization reverses measures magnetic circular dichroism.

components.name: Diamond XBPM, filters, slits, 4-ID-G entrance
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. the start of the 4-ID-G optics table, ~64.1 m on the 2021 plan.
components.text: A diamond position monitor, filter box and slits control the beam entering 4-ID-G. The filters reduce flux and the jaws limit beam area. The monitor supplies the station's feedback signal to the monochromator.

components.name: Transfocator, Be compound refractive lenses
components.distanceNote: 2 m upstream of the diffractometer, 2021 town hall. The 2021 plan shows the CRL at ~65.25 m.
components.text: Beryllium lenses focus X-rays by refraction. Each lens bends rays only slightly, so many are placed in series. Inserting more of the eight lens groups reduces focal length. Software selects the combination for the X-ray energy and desired spot. The lens system covers 3 to 20 keV and produces about 2 × 0.9 µm spots, between the toroidal-mirror and nanofocusing sizes.

components.name: KB1 nano-focusing mirrors, 100 mm from focus
components.distanceNote: Approximate. Computed from the sample at 67.2 m minus the 100 mm working distance and half-lengths of the FDR KB1 mirrors, VFM 275 mm upstream of HFM 115 mm.
components.text: Two curved Kirkpatrick-Baez mirrors focus in perpendicular directions about 100 mm before the sample. They produce roughly 100 nm beams. Their elliptical surfaces have root-mean-square shape errors below 0.5 nm. The design predicts 114 × 92 nm with 1.3 × 10¹³ photons/s at 10 keV. A slit selects coherent light for imaging, leaving 1.6 × 10¹² photons/s in a 200 × 200 nm spot.

specs.coherentMode: 200 × 200 nm² with 1.6 × 10¹² photons/s at 10 keV, using mirrors and slit

components.name: Huber diffractometer, horizontal scattering
components.distanceNote: Sample position: toroid focus point 67.2 m, 2021 town hall matches the 2021 plan, ~67.3 m. FDR 2019 had the diffractometer at 61.3 m in a different hutch arrangement.
components.text: This diffractometer rotates the sample and detectors to measure reflections from atomic and magnetic order. It operates in the horizontal plane without the usual vertical circle, leaving space for magnets and cryostats. Two detector-arm branches, separated by 25°, hold an area detector and a polarization analyzer.

specs.geometry: 4S+2D horizontal (τ, μ, χ, φ, γ, δ)

components.name: ±2 T HTS split-pair magnet, diffractometer
components.distanceNote: Mounted on the diffractometer at the sample position.
components.text: This superconducting magnet uses a closed-cycle refrigerator rather than liquid helium. It produces up to 2 T, about 40,000 times Earth's field, along or across the beam. The field can rise from zero to 2 T in five minutes. High-temperature-superconductor coils leave a 60.4 mm gap for cryostats, mini diamond cells and strain cells.

components.name: Imaging stack, dichroic ptychography
components.distanceNote: Operating position: it replaces the open Eulerian cradle on the diffractometer base at the 67.2 m sample point. The 3D model shows it parked on a cart beside the diffractometer so both configurations can be seen.
components.text: This sample-positioning assembly replaces the diffractometer cradle for coherent imaging. Its tilts and translations support a 360° air-bearing rotation and a nanometre positioner. Interferometers measure sample position relative to the beam. Forward-scattered patterns support ptychography and tomography; crystal reflections support Bragg coherent diffraction imaging. The exhibit places the assembly beside the diffractometer to show both configurations.

components.name: Vortex ME-4 fluorescence detector, SDD
components.distanceNote: At the sample. Shown looking in from the outboard side just upstream of 90°, snout ~0.17 m from the sample, through the HTS magnet's radial opening and clear of the detector arm; the exact mounting is not published.
components.text: This four-element silicon drift detector records fluorescence, the characteristic X-rays emitted after each element absorbs incident X-rays. Energy resolution separates an element's fluorescence from other emission. It supports fluorescence-detected dichroism and absorption spectroscopy and separates fluorescence background from resonant scattering.

components.name: Polarization analyzer + APD, detector arm
components.distanceNote: On the point-detector branch of the split detector arm, ~0.9 m from the sample, not published. Shown with the arm at 2θ = 60° toward the outboard side, the plan draws the ~2 m arm sweep there, which puts it 67.65 m along the beam.
components.text: An analyzer crystal reflects scattered X-rays through nearly 90° and selects one polarization for an avalanche photodiode. Charge scattering usually preserves polarization; magnetic scattering can rotate it. A reflection in the rotated channel is therefore evidence of magnetic scattering. The crystal is selected for the element's absorption-edge energy.

specs.analyzerCrystals: PG(001), Cu, Au, Al, Si, Ge, LiF, MgO, Mo, Pd, Pt …

components.name: Eiger2 X 1M pixel detector, also Lambda 750k
components.distanceNote: Variable 0.5 to 2 m from the sample on the PAD branch of the arm. Shown at 1.5 m with that branch at 2θ = 35°, 25° from the analyzer branch, i.e. 68.4 m along the beam. For forward ptychography, detector distances of 2.7, 4 and 10 m are planned; 10 m would reach into 4-ID-H, unconfirmed.
components.text: This photon-counting detector has about a million pixels. It records diffraction spots and coherent scattering patterns for magnetic-domain reconstruction. On the detector arm it is 0.5 to 2 m from the sample. A Lambda 750k detector is also available.

specs.distance: 0.5 to 2 m, diffraction; 2.7/4/10 m, ptychography, planned

components.name: G/H station shutter, inferred
components.distanceNote: The inferred shutter is based on an unlabelled box near 69.6 to 69.9 m on the 2021 elevation, just before the G/H wall. Final-design Table 4.16 specifies a second shutter, 4ID-SH-2, at 64.6 m in the different 2019 layout. Identity, exact position and installation are unconfirmed.
components.text: The drawings suggest a shutter at the end of 4-ID-G, but its identity and installation are unconfirmed. In the published design, access to 4-ID-H for pressure-cell loading, magnet cooling or maintenance is possible while 4-ID-G operates. A shutter or stop at this boundary is needed for that access.

components.name: Diamond XBPM, Sydor at 4-ID-H entrance
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.16. The magnet position, 73.3 m is unchanged between FDR and as-built, so the upstream H positions are kept.
components.text: This diamond beam-position monitor supplies the 4-ID-H feedback loop. The loop adjusts the monochromator crystal to maintain beam position on the sample inside the magnet.

components.name: 4-ID-H slits
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.16, 4ID-SL-6, an existing slit.
components.text: These jaws limit the illuminated area of the focusing mirrors. The two undulators occupy different longitudinal positions and form slightly different source images. Restricting mirror illumination reduces the resulting spot asymmetry, at a cost in transmitted flux.

components.name: 4-ID-H attenuators
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.16.
components.text: These metal foils reduce flux for alignment and protect detectors and radiation-sensitive samples. They serve 4-ID-H as the filter box serves 4-ID-B.

components.name: KB2 long-working-distance mirrors, 600 mm
components.distanceNote: Approximate. FDR KB2 at 72.46 m, VFM and 72.78 m, HFM for a 400 mm WD; the as-built WD is 600 mm, so the mirrors sit ~0.2 m further upstream, computed.
components.text: The magnet body requires the Kirkpatrick-Baez mirrors to sit 60 cm from the focus. This working distance was increased from 400 to 600 mm for the 9-1-1 T magnet. The larger distance reduces demagnification, but the listed spot remains 300 to 400 nm. The design predicts 414 × 212 nm with 2.1 × 10¹³ photons/s at 10 keV.

components.name: Incident-intensity monitor I0, 4-ID-H
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.16, 4ID-BD-4, between the KB2 mirrors, ending ~72.7 m and the magnet's upstream window.
components.text: This monitor measures incident intensity before the magnet. Absorption is determined relative to that value. Other channels measure intensity downstream.

components.name: 9-1-1 T superconducting magnet, vector
components.distanceNote: Toroid focus point 73.3 m, 2021 town hall. FDR gives 73.3 to 73.4 m; the 2021 plan confirms.
components.text: This liquid-helium-cooled magnet has a 75 mm bore for the diamond anvil cell. Its split coils produce up to 9 T along the beam and 1 T along each perpendicular axis, giving the name 9-1-1. A temperature insert covers 1.4 to 300 K. Liquid helium avoids cryocooler vibration that could blur a 300 nm beam. Side ports provide fluorescence and Raman access. Interferometers measure drift during a zero-to-9 T ramp of about nine minutes. The magnet translates out of the beam to give access to the downstream 4 T magnet.

components.name: Diamond anvil cell, double gas membrane
components.distanceNote: At the centre of the magnet.
components.text: Two diamond tips compress the sample between them. The 2026 directory lists 3 megabars; the design goal is about 6 megabars. Separate helium-filled compression and decompression membranes change pressure remotely inside the cold magnet. The non-magnetic copper-beryllium cell sits on a nanopositioner that aligns the sample with the beam.

specs.pressure: 3 Mbar, operational, per directory; ~6 Mbar goal
specs.pressureControl: Helium gas membranes with remote pressure control, configured as ge_apply and ge_release in Bluesky
specs.mount: x/y/z nanopositioner at the probe tip
specs.cell: non-magnetic CuBe, compression + decompression He membranes

components.name: Raman / ruby spectrometer, pressure gauge
components.distanceNote: Optical access through the magnet's re-entrant side bore on the outboard side, SRI 2021 drawing.
components.text: A laser and spectrometer measure pressure through a side port. Below 100 GPa, or 1 megabar, pressure shifts the ruby fluorescence wavelength. Above this range, the gauge uses the Raman shift of the compressed diamond tip. The instrument also supports Raman measurements of the sample.

specs.calibration: ruby, <100 GPa, diamond Raman edge, >100 GPa

components.name: Laser interferometers, sample position
components.distanceNote: Heads on the magnet support, looking into the side bores.
components.text: Interferometers measure displacement of the magnet and sample during field changes. A slow feedback loop moves the nanopositioner to restore sample alignment with the sub-micrometre beam.

components.name: 7-element fluorescence detector, SDD
components.distanceNote: At the sample, through a Be-windowed re-entrant side bore of the magnet, inboard side in the model; Raman uses the outboard bore. The FDR lists 74.2 m for the detector stand.
components.text: A seven-element silicon drift detector records sample fluorescence through a beryllium-windowed side port. This allows absorption measurements when direct transmission through the sample is unsuitable.

components.name: Transmission detector I, 4-ID-H
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.16, 4ID-BD-5.
components.text: This detector measures X-rays transmitted through the diamonds and sample. Increased absorption at an edge reduces transmission. The change when circular polarization reverses supplies the magnetic-dichroism signal.

components.name: 4 T cryogen-free magnet, existing
components.distanceNote: Approximate, from the 2021 plan, ~76.3 m; the FDR gives 75.9 m, 'small-bore 4 T magnet, existing'.
components.text: This cryogen-free 4 T magnet was retained from 4-ID-D at the end of the beamline. Moving the 9-1-1 T magnet out of the beam allows it to operate. The toroidal mirrors provide a beam tens of micrometres across. The nanofocusing mirrors focus at the upstream magnet, too far upstream for a nanofocus here.

components.name: Beam stop, 4ID-BS-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.16; the 2021 plan shows it at ~77.6 m, at the downstream wall of 4-ID-H.
components.text: This dense block absorbs the remaining beam at the downstream wall of 4-ID-H.

enclosures.name: 4-ID-A
enclosures.role: First optics enclosure. Front-end exit table, white-beam slits, high-heat-load mirrors, vertical monochromator, collimators, phase-retarder tank and monochromatic shutter.
enclosures.notes: Boundaries are scaled from the 2021 town-hall 'Sector 4 2024' plan with ±0.3 m uncertainty and are consistent with the 2017 preliminary-design drawing. This enclosure contains white and pink beam. Optics installation was planned for April to August 2023. The outer height is about 3.4 m, scaled from slide 16 with ±0.3 m uncertainty, assuming the elevation and metre axis use the same scale. The ratchet wall forms the inboard side. Interior width increases from about 1.6 m upstream to 2.2 m downstream on the plan.

enclosures.name: Shielded transport
enclosures.role: Lead-shielded vacuum pipe on the experiment floor. This is beam transport rather than an enclosure.
enclosures.notes: The existing transport appears in the 2017 preliminary design and 2021 town-hall plan. An earlier exhibit draft called it 'U1-40'; that label is absent from the published drawings.

enclosures.name: 4-ID-MH
enclosures.role: Legacy mini-hutch on the transport line
enclosures.notes: This mini-hutch appears on the 2021 Sector 4 plan. Its current contents and function are undocumented in the sources reviewed. Outer height is about 2.0 m, scaled from slide 16 with ±0.3 m uncertainty, assuming the elevation and metre axis use the same scale. Width is about 1.2 m on the plan.

enclosures.name: 4-ID-B
enclosures.role: Existing experimental enclosure, modified for POLAR. Toroidal and cylindrical focusing mirrors for G and H, diamond window, polarimeter, beam-position monitor, chopper, KB3 mirrors and 2 T electromagnet station.
enclosures.notes: The former 4-ID-B white- and monochromatic-beam station was retained, with manual and pneumatic double doors added outboard. Plan-scaled width is about 2.5 m, increasing to 2.9 m in places before the outboard wall tapers inward downstream. Outer height is about 3.4 m, scaled from the 2021 town-hall elevation on slide 16 with ±0.3 m uncertainty, assuming the elevation and metre axis use the same scale. The toroidal mirrors focus for 4-ID-G and 4-ID-H. Beam for these stations passes through 4-ID-B.

enclosures.name: 4-ID control room
enclosures.role: Control room on the outboard side alongside 4-ID-B
enclosures.notes: On the 2021 plan, racks are level with the upstream wall of 4-ID-B at about 52.8 m. Operator desks are at about 60 to 63.4 m outboard, between 4-ID-B and the existing XTIP control rooms A and B. These remeasured positions replace the research dossier's first estimate of 58 to 68 m.

enclosures.name: 4-ID-G
enclosures.role: New experimental enclosure. Transfocator, KB1 mirrors and Huber diffractometer for resonant scattering, reflectivity and dichroic imaging.
enclosures.notes: The enclosure was built during the upgrade shutdown on the former 4-ID-D and closed 4-ID-C floor area. The 2021 plan scheduled construction for September to December 2023 and instrument installation for January to April 2024. A double door is outboard. The detector-arm sweep has a drawn radius of about 2 m. Plan-scaled width is about 4.6 m. Outer height is about 4.2 m, scaled from the town-hall elevation on slide 16 with ±0.3 m uncertainty, assuming the elevation and metre axis use the same scale.

enclosures.name: 4-ID-H
enclosures.role: New experimental enclosure. KB2 mirrors, 9-1-1 T magnet with diamond cell and Raman spectrometer, 4 T magnet and beam stop.
enclosures.notes: Double doors are outboard and at the downstream inboard corner. A platform and stairs provide top access for the magnet insert, beside a liquid-helium dewar position. The outboard wall angles inward downstream. The 2017 preliminary design required a 6 m ceiling for vertical loading; the as-built height is unconfirmed. The 2021 town-hall elevation on slide 16 gives about 6.2 m when scaled with the metre axis, with ±0.3 m uncertainty. That drawn height is consistent with the 6 m requirement.

instruments.name: Phase-retarder polarization control system
instruments.text: Three plate stages control polarization in transmission. Two carry diamond and one thin silicon for the lowest energies. Their reflection planes lie 45° to the incident polarization. Plate angles follow the monochromator and undulator settings as energy changes. Piezo modulation reverses the circular polarization, and lock-in detection measures the small absorption difference. Circular polarization is about 98%; vertical linear polarization is also available with two plates. The working range is about 2.7 to 14 keV. The system is intended to remain as a backup after a polarizing undulator is commissioned.

instruments.name: 2 T electromagnet XMCD station
instruments.text: A water-cooled electromagnet retained from the old beamline is used for magnetic absorption spectroscopy on films, crystals, powders and lightly compressed samples. Adjustable Kirkpatrick-Baez mirrors focus the beam. Photodiodes measure transmission or fluorescence as the field reverses. Its design range is below 1 megabar, above 10 K and about 0.8 T with a diamond cell. It is configured in the control software but absent from the 2026 endstation directory. Its availability to users is unconfirmed.
detectors: Photodiodes or ion chambers for incident and transmitted intensity, I0 and I

instruments.name: Huber diffractometer with 2 T HTS magnet
instruments.text: This diffractometer rotates crystals and films for magnetic diffraction, reflectivity and absorption measurements. A 2 T magnet surrounds the sample. The split arm carries a pixel detector 0.5 to 2 m away and a polarization analyzer with an avalanche photodiode. A side-mounted fluorescence detector records element-specific emission. Temperatures cover 4 to 450 K. Mini diamond cells, strain cells and voltage bias are supported. The in-vacuum option reaches 2.75 keV for circular dichroism and resonant reflectivity at 4d-metal L edges.

instruments.name: Dichroic coherent-imaging setup
instruments.text: An air-bearing rotation and nanopositioner replace the diffractometer cradle for 2D and 3D magnetic imaging. Mirrors 100 mm from the focus provide a coherent beam of about 100 nm. Interferometers measure sample position. Planned forward-ptychography detector distances are 2.7, 4 and 10 m; Bragg coherent imaging uses 2 m. A 2021 Argonne internal research grant supported development of the 3D method. General-user availability of these modes in 2026 is unconfirmed.
sampleEnvironments: Room temperature or small electromagnet; other environments under development

instruments.name: 9-1-1 T magnet and diamond anvil cell
instruments.text: This instrument combines high pressure, low temperature and magnetic field. A gas-membrane copper-beryllium diamond anvil cell sits on a nanopositioner inside the 9-1-1 T vector magnet. The temperature range is 1.4 to 300 K. Kirkpatrick-Baez mirrors focus from 600 mm away. Interferometers measure drift; ruby fluorescence and Raman spectroscopy measure pressure. A seven-element detector records fluorescence through a side port, and a downstream window permits diffraction. Circular dichroism uses up to 9 T along the beam. Linear dichroism uses 1 T across it. The directory lists 3 megabars and 8.7 T for this instrument.
detectors: Ion chambers or photodiodes for I0, I1 and I2
sampleEnvironments: Diamond anvil cell with helium membranes. Operational pressure 3 Mbar; goal 6 Mbar.

instruments.name: 4 T cryogen-free magnet
instruments.text: A retained refrigerator-cooled 4 T magnet with a small bore sits at the end of the line. It came from 4-ID-D. For operation, the upstream 9-1-1 T magnet moves aside in 'beam-pass' mode. The beam is then focused by the toroidal mirrors into a broader spot.

instruments.name: Planned MagXES spectrometer
instruments.text: MagXES is a planned magnetic X-ray emission spectrometer for low temperature, high pressure and high field. It would measure local magnetic states through sample emission. A 2024 US Department of Energy Early Career award to G. Fabbris funds the instrument. Its design, location and schedule are unpublished.

geometryNotes:
POLAR uses two collinear planar undulators and a phase shifter on one non-canted beamline. Before the upgrade, sector 4 had canted sources for soft-X-ray 4-ID-C, with its CPU undulator, and 4-ID-E/XTIP, plus hard-X-ray 4-ID-D. POLAR now occupies the whole straight. Sources are APS News 2020, the 2021 POLAR town hall and Srajer 2002.

The high-heat-load mirror pair reflects horizontally at 3 mrad grazing incidence per mirror. It returns the beam parallel with about 4 mm lateral offset; the direction is unpublished. The vertical monochromator adds a fixed 15.6 mm offset, assumed upward in the exhibit. Phase plates transmit along the beam, with their diffraction planes rolled 45°. The M3/M4 pair at 53.7/54.5 m reflects horizontally at 2 to 4 mrad per mirror and produces a lateral offset of a few millimetres. It retracts for KB and refractive-lens focusing. The downstream axes therefore differ slightly between focusing modes. Each KB pair has a vertical mirror followed by a horizontal mirror, both at 3 mrad.

Enclosure bounds were scaled from the 2021 'Sector 4 2024' plan with ±0.3 m uncertainty. The first hutch, 4-ID-A, spans 24.4 to 36.1 m against the ratchet wall. Shielded transport covers 36.1 to 50.5 m, and mini-hutch 4-ID-MH covers 50.5 to 52.8 m. Existing 4-ID-B spans 52.8 to 63.3 m, is about 2.5 m wide and tapers downstream. New 4-ID-G spans 63.5 to 70.0 m; 4-ID-H spans 70.0 to 77.7 m. Both are about 4.6 m wide, with H's outboard wall angled inward downstream. All stand on the experiment-hall floor.

The control room is outboard of B next to the XTIP rooms. In the 2021 plan, racks align with B's upstream wall and desks occupy about 60 to 63 m. B, G and H have outboard double doors; H has another double door at its downstream inboard corner. Stairs and a loading platform serve the 9-1-1 magnet, which translates inboard to pass beam downstream. The neighbouring 5-BM hutches are inboard.

The 2017 Preliminary Design Report placed instruments in 4-ID-B and 4-ID-D. The 2019 Final Design Report used 4-ID-E for the second optics enclosure, with the diffractometer at 61.3 m in B and the magnet at 73.3 m in G. From the 2021 redesign, the diffractometer is in new G at about 67.2 m and the magnet in new H at 73.3 m. The dossiers use those later names.

Slide 16 of the 2021 town hall sketches an upward monochromator offset and an inboard offset from M1/M2. These directions are inferred from a schematic rather than an engineering drawing. Heights scaled from its elevation are about 3.4 m for A and B, 2.0 m for MH, 4.2 m for G and 6.2 m for H. Beam height is about 1.4 m above the floor. All have ±0.3 m scaling uncertainty.

The exhibit uses one beam axis because the 4 mm mirror, 15.6 mm monochromator and few-millimetre toroid offsets cannot be seen at hall scale. M1 is mounted outboard and reflects inboard, following the schematic. Positions follow the 2021 plan rather than the earlier FDR table where they differ, including the monochromator at 30.6 m and phase retarders at 33.45 m.

The near walls and roofs are omitted to expose the equipment. Phase plates are enlarged about 7 times in an open tank. Their 45° diffraction-plane roll is drawn at the optically equivalent 225°. The see-through 9-1-1 T cryostat and a cutaway in its 9 T coils expose the diamond cell. The anvils are enlarged about 2 times. The imaging stage is parked beside the diffractometer, whose detector branches are at 2θ = 60°/35°. Polarization arrows have a 0.32 m period and slowed reversals for visibility.

interactiveIdeas.title: Circular polarization from a diamond plate
interactiveIdeas.concept: Visitors tilt a virtual diamond plate a few tens of arcseconds from its Bragg angle. Arrows represent the two perpendicular electric-field components, σ and π, at 45° to the reflection plane. Their phase difference changes as the plate tilts. The resulting field traces a line, an ellipse or a circle. Tilting to the other side reverses the rotation direction. A 'flip' button changes the piezo tilt at the 15 Hz design rate. An energy slider shows the required angular offset falling at higher energy and polarization degrading above about 14 keV.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: A perfect crystal delays perpendicular electric-field components by different amounts. This changes linear polarization into circular polarization. Mechanical tilting reverses the helicity. Source-generated polarization is planned for energies from 14 to 27 keV, beyond the useful phase-plate range.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: For a Bragg-transmission phase retarder, δ(Δθ) = (π/2)·Δθq/Δθ. The quarter-wave offset is Δθq = 2·t·cosθB·r_e²·λ³·Re(F_h·F_h̄)/(π²·V²), following the APS-4ID-POLAR Pharet calculator. A derived example uses C(111), t = 500 µm and 10 keV, with θB = 17.5°, |F|² = 32 f², f_C ≈ 3.0 and V = 45.4 Å³. It gives Δθq ≈ 2 × 10⁻⁴ rad ≈ 42″. Circular fraction Pc = sin δ; opposite offsets give opposite helicity. Two plates giving δ = π produce vertical linear polarization. Divergence and bandwidth reduce circular purity unless their angular spread is much smaller than the offset. Bandwidth ΔE/E ≈ 1.4 × 10⁻⁴ corresponds to Δθ = tanθB·ΔE/E. Haskel 2018 and the 2017 preliminary design give five- to thirtyfold transmission loss over 2.8 to 14 keV, and 5 to 30% intensity asymmetry between helicities. The plate reflection plane must be 45° to incident polarization.

interactiveIdeas.title: Magnetic circular dichroism at an absorption edge
interactiveIdeas.concept: Visitors select an element, Fe K, Gd L3, Ir L3 or U M5, and a magnetized sample. Absorption curves for left and right circular polarization appear. Their difference measures magnetic circular dichroism. Reversing the field or helicity reverses the difference. A noise slider compares slow scans with 15 Hz switching and lock-in detection.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Absorption-edge measurements distinguish elements. Reversing polarization separates sub-percent magnetic changes from other absorption and drift.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Use μ± = μ0·(1 ± Pc·cosφ·A(E)), with φ the angle between helicity and magnetization. Haskel and colleagues give hard-X-ray XMCD amplitudes from 0.1 to 6% of the edge jump in 2007. The 2017 design target is about 10 ppm. At L2,3, the sum rules are m_orb ∝ ∫(ΔμL3 + ΔμL2) and m_spin + 7⟨T_z⟩ ∝ ∫ΔμL3 − 2∫ΔμL2, following Thole and colleagues, 1992. A 0.1 µrad source-angle change shifts Si(111) energy by about 3 meV at 8 keV in the preliminary-design calculation. Reverse polarization at each energy point to limit the resulting artefact. X-ray Data Booklet edge energies are Fe K 7.112, Gd L3 7.243, Ir L3 11.215 and U M5 3.552 keV.

interactiveIdeas.title: Beam size and pressure in a diamond cell
interactiveIdeas.concept: Visitors change the tip diameter in a two-diamond press. Pressure rises as the tips shrink, but so does the sample area. The gauge marks 100 GPa = 1 Mbar ≈ 0.6 eV/Å³, using 1 eV/Å³ ≈ 160 GPa, and about 3.6 Mbar at Earth's centre. Overlaid beams compare the old roughly 15 µm spot, which extends onto the metal gasket, with POLAR's 0.3 µm spot. A perforated-anvil option changes X-ray transmission.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Higher pressure requires smaller diamond tips and samples. A smaller beam fits within the sample. POLAR's pressure goal is about ten times its predecessor's range. Hard X-rays penetrate diamond more readily than soft X-rays.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Pressure P = F/A increases as diamond-tip area decreases. Perforated anvils require about half the culet diameter for a given pressure in the 2017 design. That design specifies about 1 µm beam width for 3 to 4 Mbar and treats 6 to 7 Mbar as a practical static-compression limit. Double-stage cells have reported higher pressure, near 1 TPa, in tiny samples with debated calibration, as in Dubrovinskaia and colleagues, 2016, cited at the 2021 town hall. Transmission is T = exp(−μL). Haskel and colleagues, 2007, quote attenuation greater than 10¹² through 100 µm diamond over 0.5 to 1.5 keV. NIST values are about 5 × 10¹⁰ at 1.5 keV and 10³⁴ at 1 keV. Through 1 mm diamond at the iron K edge, 7.1 keV, attenuation is only about tenfold. Partially perforated anvils leave about 0.1 to 0.2 mm diamond. Ruby calibration is used below 100 GPa and the diamond Raman edge above it.

interactiveIdeas.title: Absorption edges within the energy range
interactiveIdeas.concept: Visitors select an element on a periodic table to view its K, L or M absorption edges within 2.7 to 27 keV. Phase-plate polarization is available from about 2.7 to 14 keV. Circular polarization above about 14 keV awaits a polarizing undulator. In the higher SCAPE harmonics, elliptical polarization with a circular fraction of about 75 to 90% is planned. The display marks silicon-carbide optics near 2.8 keV, rare-earth L3 edges at 5.5 to 9.2 keV with L2 up to 10.3 keV, 5d L3 edges at 9.6 to 11.9 keV with L2 up to 13.7 keV, actinide M4,5 edges at 3.3 to 4 keV and actinide L2,3 edges at 16.3 to 22.3 keV.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Resonant X-ray measurements distinguish elements by their absorption edges. The available energy and polarization determine which edges are accessible.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Use X-ray Data Booklet edge values. Examples in keV are Ru L3 2.838, Pd L3 3.173, U M4 3.728, Ce L3 5.723, Gd L3 7.243, Yb L3 8.944, Ir L3 11.215, Pt L3 11.564, U L3 17.166, Pu L3 18.057 and Ru K 22.117. The undulator formula E1 [keV] = 0.950·E²[GeV]/(λu[cm]·(1 + K²/2)) gives about 2.57 keV for K = 2.62, period 3 cm and 6 GeV. The insertion-device table gives 2.56 keV. Higher-energy emission peaks are odd harmonics.

interactiveIdeas.title: Polarization near a 45° Bragg angle
interactiveIdeas.concept: Visitors rotate a monochromator crystal. The reflected π component, with its electric field in the reflection plane, falls to zero as the Bragg angle passes 45°. For Si(111), this occurs at about 2.8 keV. With 6H-SiC(0006), the angle at this energy is 61.4°, so this component is transmitted through the monochromator by reflection.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Near 45°, crystal reflection strongly suppresses one polarization. Silicon-carbide crystals avoid this condition near the absorption edges of the 4d metals ruthenium, rhodium and palladium.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: The kinematic polarization factors are 1 for σ and |cos 2θB| for π. The dynamical π Darwin width also scales with |cos 2θB|. For Si(111), d = 3.1356 Å gives a 45° Bragg angle at 2.796 keV. For 6H-SiC(0006), d = 2.522 Å gives 61.4° at 2.8 keV. Silicon-carbide Darwin width is about 0.29 eV with peak reflectivity about 74% at 2.8 keV in the preliminary design, Strempfer and colleagues' 2022 paper and 2021 town hall. The polarization factor matters for source-generated vertical linear or circular light. Phase-plate polarization is produced after the monochromator; the vertical monochromator reflects the original horizontal polarization as σ.

interactiveIdeas.title: Magnetic imaging with ptychography
interactiveIdeas.concept: Visitors scan a coherent spot across magnetic domains. A scattering pattern is recorded at each position. A 'reconstruct' button runs a simplified iterative algorithm. Images reconstructed for left and right circular polarization are subtracted to map the domains. A slider compares coherence before and after the APS upgrade and its effect on reconstruction.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: With coherent X-rays, images are reconstructed from overlapping diffraction measurements at a resolution finer than the beam size. Circular dichroism adds contrast from magnetism.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Scan overlap should be at least 60%. Approximate resolution is λ·z/(N·p), limited by detector numerical aperture and dose. It is independent of the nominal beam width. Coherent fraction per direction is approximately (λ/4π)/(Σ·Σ'). The 2023 workshop gives roughly two hundredfold gain at 10 keV. Strempfer and colleagues give 1.6 × 10¹² coherent photons/s in 200 nm. Magnetic contrast is the complex-transmission difference between opposite helicities. Three-dimensional vector tomography requires at least two rotation axes, following Donnelly and colleagues, 2017.

interactiveIdeas.title: Polarization reversal and drift
interactiveIdeas.concept: Visitors compare helicity-reversal times. The 2002 soft-X-ray circularly polarizing undulator took about five minutes. Diamond phase plates operate at about 13 to 40 Hz. The SCAPE orbit-bump scheme has a planned rate of at least 10 Hz, and X-undulator schemes specify 1 to 5 Hz. The display illustrates absorption drift during slower measurements and its effect on a small magnetic difference.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Polarization reversal separates magnetic absorption from drift when the reversal is faster than the relevant drift.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Srajer reported about five-minute helicity reversal for the circularly polarizing undulator in 2002. Phase-plate rates are typically 12.7 to 15 Hz in Haskel and colleagues, 2007, and the 2021 town hall; Srajer reported up to 40 Hz. The planned SCAPE orbit scheme uses about 30 µrad changes, at least 95% polarization purity and 10 Hz reversal. Qian and colleagues' 2024 X-undulator scheme specifies 7.5 mm quarter-period motion at 1 Hz, or 5 Hz with detuning of two X-undulators.

funFacts: Piezo tilt reverses the circular polarization of X-rays transmitted through diamond. The POLAR 2021 town-hall design specifies about 15 reversals per second. Haskel and colleagues reported 12.7 Hz for the 2007 high-pressure instrument.
Helicity reversal for Sector 4's soft-X-ray circularly polarizing undulator took about five minutes in 2002, according to Srajer.
The 9-1-1 T magnet uses liquid helium rather than a mechanical cryocooler. Cryocooler vibration could blur a 300 nm beam, as discussed by Strempfer and colleagues in 2022.

At the iron absorption edge of 7.1 keV, 1 mm of diamond reduces X-ray transmission by about tenfold. For soft X-rays, just 0.1 mm reduces transmission by about 5 × 10¹⁰ at 1.5 keV and 10³⁴ at 1 keV. These values follow Haskel and colleagues' 2007 discussion and NIST attenuation tables.
The 2017 preliminary design described the predecessor 4-ID-D as the only hard-X-ray XMCD beamline in the United States. Requests for beamtime exceeded availability by a factor of 3 to 4.

The pressure goal of about 6 Mbar is about 1.6 times Earth's central pressure of roughly 3.6 Mbar. The sources are the 2021 POLAR town hall and the 1981 Preliminary Reference Earth Model by Dziewonski and Anderson.

A source-angle change of just 0.1 microradian shifts monochromator energy by about 3 meV at 8 keV. Such a shift can produce an apparent magnetic difference. The 2017 preliminary design therefore specifies polarization reversal at every energy point.

The two undulators would emit about 20.6 kW at their 9.0 mm design minimum gap, close to the front-end limit of 21 kW. User gaps are at least 9.1 to 9.4 mm, according to the September 2026 insertion-device table and 2019 final design.
Endstation labels changed during design. Experiments were assigned to '4-ID-B/4-ID-D' in 2017, '4-ID-B/4-ID-G' in 2019 and '4-ID-G/4-ID-H' in the 2021 layout.
POLAR entered the upgrade scope in July 2016 following a proposal by 15 scientists from US universities and national laboratories. This history appears in the 2021 town hall and Haskel's 2024 CV.
The first POLAR users, in the January to May 2025 run, were from the University of Wisconsin. They studied flexomagnetism, magnetism induced by bending, according to APS News in June 2025.
Planned ptychography detector distances extend to 10 m, longer than the 4-ID-G hutch. These distances are from the 2023 POLAR workshop slides.
X-ray magnetic circular dichroism was first observed at the iron K edge in 1987 by Schütz and colleagues. POLAR uses hard-X-ray absorption edges of this type.
The POLAR First Experiments Workshop on 28 June 2023 opened the APS upgrade series of feature-beamline first-experiments workshops. APS News announced it in April 2023.

The directory lists 3 Mbar and 8.7 T for the diamond-cell instrument, compared with a 6 Mbar pressure goal and 9 T magnet specification. The variable-temperature insert bore is 74 mm in SRI 2022 and 3 inches, or 7.5 cm, in the slides.

General-user availability of dichroic ptychography and tomography is unconfirmed. The directory lists 'dichroic imaging, 400 nm resolution' and 'dichroic ptychography'. The locations of planned 4 m and 10 m detector positions are unpublished; they may extend into 4-ID-H.
The function of mini-hutch 4-ID-MH at 50.5 to 52.8 m and the hutch ceiling heights are unconfirmed. The PDR requests a 6 m magnet-hutch ceiling.

The earlier soft-X-ray programs have no confirmed relocation record. Closure of 4-ID-C was planned for April 2021. Converting the canted straight removed the 4-ID-E XTIP SX-STM source. A 2025 APS photograph shows the former 4-ID-C scientist performing soft-X-ray XMCD at 29-ID, but no formal relocation statement was found.
MagXES instrument design, location within POLAR and schedule are unknown.
APS News identifies the first users as a Wisconsin-Madison flexomagnetism team. Connecting them to the Kawasaki group's GdAuGe work is an inference.
A shutter or stop is required at the G/H boundary to permit H access while G operates. Its identity is unconfirmed. The exhibit places an inferred shutter at about 69.7 m.
Installation and use of the 6H-SiC(0006) monochromator crystals in 2026 are unconfirmed. They are needed only for source-generated polarization near 2.8 keV.
